name: HILLSHAPES-catalogue-mound
new: [id, () => hillMesh({ ...RMBRP_HILL_SHAPES[id], top: 1.6, reach: RMBRP_HILL_SHAPES[id].reach.map(() => 10), rings: RMBRP_HILL_SHAPES[id].rings.map((r) => r.map((h, j) => (j === r.length - 1 ? h : 1.6 * (1 - j / r.length)))) }, surface)]
note: the catalogue's 10 m, 1.6 m mound again: Ipsham's houses hang over it

name: HILLSHAPES-reach-halved
old: const b = k % K, a = (b / K) * Math.PI * 2, r = (shape.reach[b] * j) / N;
new: const b = k % K, a = (b / K) * Math.PI * 2, r = (shape.reach[b] * j) / N / 2;
note: a hill half its measured reach

name: HILLSHAPES-ring-shifted
old: return [cx + Math.cos(a) * r, shape.rings[b][j - 1], cz + Math.sin(a) * r];
new: return [cx + Math.cos(a) * r, shape.rings[b][Math.min(j, N - 1)], cz + Math.sin(a) * r];
note: each ring a ring further out's height

name: HILLSHAPES-unmirrored
old: return [cx + Math.cos(a) * r, shape.rings[b][j - 1], cz + Math.sin(a) * r];
new: return [-(cx + Math.cos(a) * r), shape.rings[b][j - 1], cz + Math.sin(a) * r];
note: the hill mirrored back across x: the profile no longer stands where the pack's surface does

name: HILLSHAPES-centre-dropped
note: a pit at the hill's centre

name: HILLSHAPES-faces-down
note: every face turned down: the hill seen from above is its back

name: HILLSHAPES-cell-one-triangle
old: else { face(a, b, c); face(a, c, d); }
note: half of every cell out to the rim left open
